items.title: The Christchurch terrorist who pleaded guilty to mass murder has changed his mind
items.description: Extraordinary arrangements are in place in Wellington, New Zealand, as a convicted terrorist prepares to address the country's Court of Appeal.

items.title: Coalition reunited after last-minute deal
items.description: The Liberals and Nationals have reached a breakthrough deal to reunite the Coalition after 11th-hour talks.

items.title: Next federal budget to 'lift speed limit' on economy, treasurer says
items.description: Treasurer Jim Chalmers says the federal government's budget in May will focus on productivity, spending restraint and tax reform.

items.title: Extra police powers ahead of Israel president protest set for legal challenge
items.description: The Palestine Action Group is set to urgently file proceedings in the NSW Supreme Court after the government declared large parts of Sydney a "major event area".

items.title: Brisbane star Payne Haas signs three-year deal with South Sydney
items.description: South Sydney have pulled off one of the biggest recruitment moves in NRL history after signing Brisbane enforcer Payne Haas to a three-year contract from 2027.

items.title: 'Could have been avoided': Backpacker's grieving parents call for action
items.description: Piper James's parents are leaving Australia to return to Vancouver with their daughter's ashes and a determination to ensure she hasn't died in vain.

items.title: Daytime power prices have never been lower. So why are bills rising?
items.description: The benefits of extremely low energy prices during the day are "washed away" by extremely high ones after dark. But there is light at the end of the tunnel.

items.title: 'This is valuable to us, and we will pay': TV host agrees to ransom demand
items.description: In a video posted to Instagram, the host of NBC's Today Show appears to directly address her mother's kidnappers, telling them she and her siblings have "received your message, and we understand".

items.title: The slow death of Starmer's prime ministership after Mandelson's 'betrayal'
items.description: Starmer's decision to hand the plum job of UK ambassador in Washington to Lord Peter Mandelson, despite knowing Mandelson had maintained a friendship with Jeffrey Epstein well past Epstein's conviction for soliciting underage prostitution, may simply be too large an error of judgement for the public to accept.

items.title: In the Australian outback listening for nuclear tests is more important than ever
items.description: As the New START treaty curbing the US and Russian nuclear weapons programs expires, the work we do here in the red centre has become more important than ever before.

items.title: Before Steve Irwin, there was Alby Mangels. This is why you no longer hear his name
items.description: In the 1980s, Alby Mangels was a box office star. The filmmaker wowed Australian audiences with his exotic adventures, but at the height of his fame he disappeared. In a rare interview he reveals what went wrong.

items.title: Man dead, five hospitalised at Sydney dance festival
items.description: Several people suffered "medical episodes" at the trance music festival at Sydney's Olympic Park, according to police.

items.title: Stakes enormous as Australia considers DNA screening for newborns
items.description: From rare cancers caught early to dementia foretold decades in advance, newborn genomic testing raises an unsettling question: Just because we can know, should we?

items.title: Retinol is booming, but doctors don't recommend it for pregnant women
items.description: Retinoids are called the "gold standard of skincare" but advice about their safety for pregnant women — even in over-the-counter skincare products like retinol — is not clear.

items.title: Family pays tribute to 'beautiful boy' who 'spread his wings one last time'
items.description: The father of an 18-year-old has paid tribute to his "beautiful boy", after a fatal plane crash south of Adelaide on Friday.

items.title: How the Liberals will justify Sussan Ley's ousting
items.description: A permission structure has been crafted for Liberals to ditch the first woman to lead the federal party room before she has even had a year in the role.

items.title: When they were told kids 'didn't read' in this town, they opened a bookshop anyway
items.description: In one of Australia's most disadvantaged regions, more known for its lead than its literature, a couple wanted to open a book store but were told children didn't read books there. They did it anyway, and it went on to become a "world class" institution.

items.title: 'Mixed feelings' about a viral trend embracing Chinese culture
items.description: Some Chinese Australians have mixed feelings about the sudden global embrace of Chinese culture after the trend emerged late last year.

items.title: Valentino Guseli's 'massive personal win' during big air final
items.description: It was 18 months ago that Valentino Guseli blew out his ACL attempting a backside 1800 at the Beijing big air. At the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Olympics snowboard big air final, he put that ghost to rest.

items.title: As West wakes up to the Epstein class, China plans global reserve currency
items.description: As the West reacts to the revelations in the latest batch of Epstein files, China has plans for the renminbi to become a global reserve currency.

items.title: Search effort winds down for missing Gold Coast fisherman
items.description: The cross-border search for a 44-year-old fisherman missing off the Gold Coast for three days has been scaled back and transitioned into a recovery phase after his boat and EPIRB were found but there were no signs of life.

items.title: $3.2m worth of illegal tobacco seized in Tasmania as new laws announced
items.description: The Tasmanian government announces increased penalties for those caught selling illegal tobacco products.

items.title: How two WA photographers captured the end of an era in gold prospecting
items.description: In 1989, two photographers travelled from Fremantle to Western Australia's Goldfields to capture the end of a gold mining era.

items.title: 3 Doors Down frontman Brad Arnold dies after cancer battle
items.description: Brad Arnold, a founder and the lead singer of American rock band 3 Doors Down, dies nine months after revealing he had kidney cancer.

items.title: $203 million crackdown on dodgy NDIS doctors now targeting veterans
items.description: Fraudsters taking advantage of people with disability now appear to be targeting veterans, prompting a $200 million crackdown by the federal government.
